I'll pull your intents and recent payments to see what's going on.
**Short answer: your instinct is right, but there are only two payments, so "suspicious" is as far as the data goes.**

**The intent:** `0x4e08…bcf4` — "Cloud infra autopay - GPU + storage, weekly", 0.50 USDC per-tx cap, 2.00 USDC total cap, merchant locked to `0x1111…1111`.

**What it did:**

| Time (2026-09-13) | Amount | % of per-tx cap |
|---|---|---|
| 08:09:41Z | 0.49 USDC | 98% |
| 08:09:48Z | 0.49 USDC | 98% |

Two byte-identical payments to the same merchant, **7 seconds apart**, each pinned just under the ceiling.

**Why that's a flag:**
- Identical amounts sitting at 98% of the cap is the shape you'd expect if one larger charge got sliced into cap-sized pieces.
- Equally consistent with a **retry that settled twice** — a duplicate charge.
- The intent says *weekly*, but both landed in the same minute. Cadence doesn't match its own description.
- It burned **49% of the total cap** in that 7-second window. Only 0.22 USDC of funding remains, so the next 0.49 charge fails on funding before it even hits the cap — that's an outage risk for infra autopay.

**Honest caveat:** I can't tell splitting from duplication from here. Receipts exist for both payments, but the subgraph doesn't expose invoice contents, nonces, or retry flags — the one field that would settle it. And two payments in a single 65-second burst is no baseline; there's no multi-day history to compare against. The "weekly" mismatch is suggestive, not proof.

**What I'd do now:** drop the per-tx cap below 0.49 on `0x4e08`. That forces the agent to fail loudly instead of quietly settling a possible duplicate, and it costs you nothing while you check the provider's invoice for 2026-09-13. Normally 98% utilisation would mean the cap is too *tight* and should be raised — don't do that here until you've confirmed the two charges are genuinely separate obligations.

Two unrelated things the scan surfaced, worth a look when convenient:
- `0xe88b` (marketing trial) is **revoked** with **0.80 USDC stranded** — withdrawable immediately, no downside.
- `0x5682` ("General ops - discretionary") is Active with a **10 USDC cap and an empty merchant allowlist** — it can pay any address. Only 0.30 USDC funded today, so blast radius is small, but that changes the moment it's topped up. It has zero payment history, so pinning an allowlist now breaks nothing.

findings.title: Two identical 0.49 USDC payments, 7 seconds apart, both at 98% of per-tx cap
findings.detail: Intent 0x4e0866d3c7ac1acbd4058cc9a0877193e640bcf4 ('Cloud infra autopay - GPU + storage, weekly') paid merchant 0x1111...1111 exactly 0.49 USDC twice within 7 seconds (08:09:41Z and 08:09:48Z). Both sit at 98% of the 0.50 per-tx cap. Identical amounts pinned just under the ceiling are the signature of an agent splitting one charge into cap-sized slices — or of a retry that settled twice. The intent is described as weekly, yet both payments landed in the same minute, which contradicts the stated cadence. Both payments carry receipts, so the transfers are documented; what is not documented is whether they represent one obligation or two.

findings.title: Cloud infra intent burned 49% of its total cap in a single 7-second window
findings.detail: spentUsdc 0.98 against totalCapUsdc 2 means half the authorisation is gone on day one of a 30-day window. At this rate the intent exhausts its cap within two more such bursts, well before endsInDays 30. Funded 1.20 USDC leaves only 0.22 USDC unspent, so the next 0.49 charge will fail on funding before it fails on cap — an availability risk for infrastructure autopay.

findings.title: No other intent shows amount clustering — the pattern is isolated to the infra agent
findings.detail: The remaining two payments in the window are singletons at unrelated sizes and low cap utilisation: 0.20 USDC at 20% of per-tx cap on 0xe88b, and 0.10 USDC at 2% of per-tx cap on 0xb530. There is no repeated-amount behaviour outside 0x4e08, which argues the clustering is a property of the infra agent's billing or retry logic rather than a wallet-wide issue.

findings.title: Unrestricted merchant allowlist on a 10 USDC discretionary intent
findings.detail: Intent 0x5682 ('General ops agent - discretionary spend') is Active with totalCapUsdc 10, perTxCapUsdc 2 and merchantAllowlistSize 0 / unrestrictedMerchants true. It has never paid anyone (paymentCount 0, spentUsdc 0). Exposure is currently bounded by fundedUsdc 0.30, but the authorisation itself permits payment to any address up to 10 USDC the moment it is topped up. This is the largest uncontained authorisation in the set.

findings.title: 0.80 USDC idle on a revoked intent
findings.detail: Intent 0xe88b is Revoked ('Trial ended, tool not adopted') with fundedUsdc 1.00 and spentUsdc 0.20, leaving unspentFundedUsdc 0.80 stranded. This is 62% of all spend in the window sitting recoverable and doing nothing.

findings.title: Research intent authorised at 500x its observed spend
findings.detail: Intent 0xb530 carries totalCapUsdc 50 against spentUsdc 0.10 — capUsedPct 0.2 across a single payment. It alone accounts for 50 of the 67 USDC authorised wallet-wide while representing 8% of spend. The cap is not sized to any observed behaviour.

actions.rationale: Until the two 0.49 USDC charges are confirmed as distinct obligations, tightening the per-tx cap below 0.49 forces the agent to fail loudly rather than settle a possible duplicate. Do not raise the cap yet: near-100% utilisation normally means throttling, but here it coincides with two identical amounts 7 seconds apart, which is equally consistent with cap-evasion splitting. Resolve the ambiguity before widening the ceiling. This protects the 1.02 USDC of remaining cap headroom.

Intent is Revoked with the stated reason 'Trial ended, tool not adopted' and 0.80 USDC funded-but-unspent. There is no scenario in which this capital is spent; withdrawRemainder returns it immediately.

An Active intent with a 10 USDC total cap, a 2 USDC per-tx cap and an empty allowlist can pay any address. It has zero payment history, so there is no operational cost to pinning it to named merchants now. Current funding of 0.30 USDC limits today's blast radius but not tomorrow's after a top-up.

50 USDC authorised against 0.10 USDC spent across one payment (capUsedPct 0.2). Resizing the cap toward observed usage removes the single largest over-authorisation in the wallet without affecting the subscription's only recorded merchant.

dataGaps: No invoice, line-item or reference data on the two 0.49 USDC payments, so a split single charge cannot be distinguished from two legitimate charges or a duplicated retry — receipts exist but their contents are not exposed by the subgraph.

The window contains only 4 payments, all on 2026-09-13 within a ~65-second span. There is no multi-day history to establish a baseline, so 'weekly' cadence for 0x4e08 cannot be verified or contradicted beyond this single burst.
Merchant addresses (0x1111..., 0x2222..., 0x3333...) carry no identity or category labels, so it cannot be confirmed that 0x1111... is the intended cloud provider.
No nonce, retry flag or settlement status is exposed, which would immediately separate a duplicate submission from two distinct payments.
No prior-window data on 0x5682, so it is unclear whether it is newly created or long-dormant with an unrestricted allowlist.
